stories.title: Kiosk GPU-raster fix -- drop --enable-gpu-rasterization to kill the freeze class
acceptance: [Atlas RCA #1 -- CORRECTED PREMISE 2026-08-02, design-gate] --enable-gpu-rasterization is NOT in the repo or the eclipse-dashboard unit; it is a Debian/RPi-OS system default injected by the /usr/bin/chromium-browser wrapper from /etc/chromium.d/default-flags:7. FIX = ADD an override flag to the eclipse-dashboard unit ExecStart (deploy-pi.sh, repo-managed): --disable-gpu-rasterization (keep GL compositing) OR --disable-gpu (bulletproof software render, removes the whole GPU-command-buffer path). Atlas leans --disable-gpu (the Pi CPU trivially handles this 2D card UI; removes the entire failure class). Eliminates the chromium GPU command-buffer hot-loop (AllocateRingBuffer kFatalFailure, ~6M/boot) that froze the UI. RCA: offices/architect/findings/2026-08-02-pi-ui-freeze-chromium-gpu-command-buffer-hotloop.md

[PRECEDENCE -- verify, do NOT assume] the Debian wrapper runs `chromium $CHROMIUM_FLAGS "$@"`, so the ExecStart override SHOULD win over the injected default -- but VERIFY on the Pi (a wrapper-ordering surprise = silent mocked-green / IRL-miss)

[A-16 deploy-contract blind spot] chromium's base flags live in an OS-shipped /etc/chromium.d/ file the repo does not manage; add a one-line comment in deploy-pi.sh so a future chromium package upgrade re-introducing GPU raster is a known surface
installs via the existing cmp-guarded kiosk-unit step + daemon-reload; ruff/lint clean in-loop

[Atlas keyring fix 2026-08-03 -- SAME ExecStart as the GPU override] add --password-store=basic to the eclipse-dashboard kiosk ExecStart (both dashboard.service.x11 + .wayland). Root: the kiosk runs with no --password-store -> chromium uses the GNOME keyring for its Safe-Storage key; the password-protected Default keyring stays LOCKED under passwordless auto-login (pam_gnome_keyring never unlocks it), so chromium fires a repeating Authentication Required keyring popup. --password-store=basic keeps safe-storage in chromiums own wiped /tmp profile (no meaningful security downgrade for a kiosk that stores no real passwords). Atlas live-tested on the Pi; repo-unmanaged until this lands.

validationCriteria.outcome: the RUNNING chromium cmdline shows GPU rasterization effectively off (override present + winning), AllocateRingBuffer count stays ~0, chromium CPU low, display never freezes

stories.title: Kiosk watchdog -- auto-restart eclipse-dashboard when the renderer wedges
acceptance: [Atlas RCA #2] add a watchdog that detects a wedged renderer (e.g. AllocateRingBuffer error-rate spike, or a CPU-pegged chromium with no state-file-driven repaint) and restarts eclipse-dashboard to restore a fresh GPU context (the proven live mitigation)

conservative trigger: restart only on a genuine wedge, never flap under normal operation; log every restart so recurring wedges stay visible (defense-in-depth behind US-522, must not mask a still-present freeze class)
test proves the watchdog triggers a restart on a simulated wedge and no-ops under healthy operation; ruff clean in-loop

validationCriteria.action: simulate/observe a renderer wedge on the Pi
validationCriteria.outcome: eclipse-dashboard is auto-restarted and the display recovers with no human intervention; the restart is logged

conditionalOutcomes: watchdog is defense-in-depth, NOT the primary fix (US-522). It must surface recurring wedges, not silence them.
stories.goal: As the operator, I want the kiosk to recover itself if the renderer ever wedges, so the display never stays silently frozen (honest-instrument).
stories.completionNotes: SHAPE: deploy/eclipse-kiosk-watchdog.{service,timer} (30s Type=oneshot) + src/pi/display/kiosk_watchdog.py + a cmp-guarded deploy-pi.sh step called AFTER step_install_ui_kiosk_units. One tick = count 'AllocateRingBuffer' markers in eclipse-dashboard's journal over a 60s window; at >=100, `systemctl restart eclipse-dashboard.service` -- the exact mitigation Atlas proved live (fresh GPU context, markers back to 0). AC1 SIGNAL CHOICE, and it is a REFUSAL not an omission: the AC offered 'AllocateRingBuffer error-rate spike, OR a CPU-pegged chromium with no state-file-driven repaint'. I built ONLY the first. 'No repaint' is NOT observable from outside the browser (states_http_server silences per-request logging, so there is no access log to read a renderer heartbeat from, and I would not widen that token-gated server while US-525 is also in it), and the CPU half alone has no post-US-522 baseline: Atlas's 39/31/24%-wedged vs 18/9/8%-healthy figures predate --disable-gpu, and software rendering raises healthy CPU by an amount nobody has measured. A CPU threshold today would be a fabricated number (Rule 2), so the honest bound is stated in the module header, the architecture section and here: A WEDGE WITH A DIFFERENT SIGNATURE IS NOT DETECTED. If the CIO wants that coverage, the cheap grounded path is to read healthy chromium CPU during the US-522 multi-minute drill and then threshold against it -- or add a renderer heartbeat (page-side, Iris) which would make 'no repaint' genuinely observable. GROUNDING for the numbers: threshold 100/60s sits ~300x below the measured wedge rate (~500/s = ~30,000 per window) and above the measured healthy 0; window 60s follows Atlas's 2,500-per-5s figure; tick 30s = half the window (a wedge is recovered inside ~1.5 min vs the 4:42 the bench sat frozen); cooldown 180s > window so a tick can never see a pre-restart error; budget 5/hour is a stated POLICY choice, not a measurement. All five are CLI flags, so the unit retunes without a code change. AC2 NEVER-FLAP, six rules each with its own test: (1) an INACTIVE kiosk is left alone -- `systemctl restart` STARTS an inactive unit, which would usurp the splash OnSuccess hand-off (dashboard.service.x11 A-1, no [Install] by design); (2) an unreadable journal is UNCERTAIN, never a wedge (I-037); (3) the journal window is max(now-window, lastAttempt) so the errors that justified a restart cannot re-trigger the next tick; (4) cooldown; (5) an hourly restart BUDGET -- once spent the watchdog STOPS restarting, logs ERROR and exits 2 so systemd marks the unit FAILED; (6) the attempt is written to the tmpfs ledger BEFORE the restart fires, so an unwritable ledger CANCELS the restart rather than silently uncapping rules 3-5. AC2 'must not mask a still-present freeze class' is met structurally, not just by a log line: every restart logs at WARNING and says in-line that US-522 was supposed to have removed this class, and the budget converts a recurring wedge into a persistent visible FAILED unit instead of an invisible restart loop. FOOT-GUN CAUGHT + GUARDED: the ledger dir is the watchdog's OWN RuntimeDirectory=eclipse-kiosk-watchdog + RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=yes. Declaring RuntimeDirectory=eclipse-obd would have made systemd DELETE /run/eclipse-obd -- including the live states/ every emitter writes and the state server reads -- every 30s when this oneshot exits; and without Preserve=yes the ledger would evaporate each fire, leaving cooldown+budget permanently empty = a restart every tick. Both are pinned by tests and MUTATION-PROVED (I mutated the unit to RuntimeDirectory=eclipse-obd + Wants=eclipse-dashboard, watched exactly those two guards go red, then reverted and re-verified clean). PRIVILEGE: unprivileged (User=mcornelison) -- the restart rides the EXISTING polkit grant in deploy/polkit-rules/51-eclipse-service-control.rules (restart verb on eclipse-dashboard.service) so NO new privilege is added, plus SupplementaryGroups=systemd-journal so the journal read does not depend on journald's per-uid file split. That polkit grant is a two-correct-halves hazard (revoke it and every watchdog test stays green while recovery is dead on the Pi), so a test pins it. RULE 10: specs/architecture.md dashboard-kiosk section gains a 'Kiosk freeze class + wedge recovery' subsection covering BOTH US-522 (override-not-deletion, /etc/chromium.d surface -- US-522 shipped without a spec update, so this closes that too) and US-523, and I amended the A-1 hand-off paragraph, which flatly said 'No watchdog/timer' -- still true as written (nothing STARTS the dashboard) but it would read as a contradiction to the next person. SCOPE: unit_manifest.py deliberately NOT touched -- it consistently excludes timer-driven oneshots (drain-forensics, orphan-cleanup, boot-progress are all absent), so following that precedent is the non-drift choice; if PM/Atlas want the watchdog in `obdctl status all` that is a separate call. LIVE VALIDATION STILL OWED (validationCriteria = simulate/observe a wedge on the Pi): I could not exercise it on the box this iteration and did NOT fake it. Note for whoever runs it: with US-522 in place a NATURAL wedge should be unreproducible, so the drill is `--error-threshold 1` against any journal marker, or a synthetic marker via systemd-cat, and the meaningful assertion is that the restart happens, is logged, and the ledger caps repeats. GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY IN-LOOP: RED witnessed first (module absent -> ImportError); then tests/pi/display/test_kiosk_watchdog.py 43 passed, tests/deploy/test_kiosk_watchdog_install.py 18 passed, FULL tests/deploy 397 passed (I changed deploy-pi.sh, so the whole suite for that contract ran), tests/pi/ops green, ruff clean on all 3 touched Python files. PRE-EXISTING RED, NOT MINE: tests/lint/test_ralph_promise_tag_contract.py (TD-073) -- US-529 in this same sprint. TD-075 (10 project-wide ruff errors outside touched files) also still stands, so `make lint` clean was applied per-touched-file; `make` is not on PATH on this box, use `ruff check` directly.

stories.completionNotes: TD-059 STALL RECOVERY, NOT A RE-IMPLEMENTATION -- read this first. I booted into a tree where the implementation was ALREADY COMMITTED (e78c51e, 4 files, 724 insertions) but every piece of bookkeeping was missing: sprint.json still said sprint-ready/passes:false, progress.txt had no US-524 entry, ralph_agents.json still showed me active on it. That is the exact TD-059 shape US-505 documented (work done, synchronous gate + close dropped at the END of the iteration) and it is now the SIXTH sighting across sprints 69-70. Per the US-505 rule I re-ran the gate and VERIFIED rather than re-implementing. AC1 MECHANISM -- CONFIRMED LIVE, and the answer was NOT the one the AC's wording assumed: the AC says 'boot cmdline/config' and offers config.txt OR cmdline.txt. On the live Pi (10.27.27.100, Pi 5 Rev 1.1) /proc/cmdline carries NO cma= arg at all -- the 64 MiB pool comes from the DEVICE TREE (dmesg: 'created CMA memory pool ... size 64 MiB' against the linux,cma reserved-memory node) -- and /boot/firmware/config.txt holds a bare `dtoverlay=vc4-kms-v3d` at line 26. So the mechanism is the OVERLAY PARAM (cma-256, documented in the Pi's own /boot/firmware/overlays/README as cma-64..cma-512), not a cmdline edit. That choice is also the RECOVERABLE one and that is why it was taken: a bad overlay param makes the firmware skip the overlay (dark display, SSH still up) whereas a malformed cmdline.txt can break root= and leave an UNBOOTABLE HEADLESS box. A guard pins that cmdline.txt is never touched. AC1 SECOND HALF -- deploy-pi.sh CAN write it within scope, so the conditionalOutcome escape hatch ('emit a one-line CIO ops instruction instead') was correctly NOT taken: there is an exact precedent in step_enforce_eeprom_power_off_on_halt (US-253), a standalone sudo'd idempotent script re-asserted on EVERY deploy. step_set_gpu_cma mirrors it verbatim and is ordered directly after it, both AFTER sync_tree so the script exists on the Pi. Re-asserting every deploy is the point, not redundancy: config.txt is OS-shipped and rewritable out-of-band by rpi-update / an image upgrade / raspi-config -- the same unmanaged-boot-surface class as US-522's /etc/chromium.d note (A-16). NEW VERIFICATION I ADDED THIS ITERATION (the original commit did not have it): I ran set-gpu-cma.sh against a COPY of the live Pi's REAL config.txt, not only my synthetic fixtures. This matters because the real file turns out to contain [cm4], [cm5] (with its own dtoverlay=dwc2,dr_mode=host) and [all] sections -- so the script's section-scoping logic is LIVE-RELEVANT, not hypothetical: config.txt is section-conditional, and appending cma to a line under [cm4] would be a false 'applied' claim on a Pi 5. Result against the real file: applied cleanly at line 26 -> `dtoverlay=vc4-kms-v3d,cma-256`; idempotent no-op on re-run; backup pristine (no cma); and the [cm5] dwc2 overlay UNTOUCHED, which is the proof it does not spray cma- onto unrelated overlays. Probe ran on a COPY only -- the Pi's real boot config was never modified (read-only `cat` was the only remote op) -- and all four temp files were deleted + the deletion verified. AC2 IS GENUINELY OWED, AND I DID NOT FAKE IT: 'verify post-boot CmaTotal reflects the raise' needs the deploy + a REBOOT, and deploying is PM-owned (handbook 13), not Ralph's. I probed read-only and report the honest current state: the Pi is STILL at CmaTotal 65536 kB, the overlay line is still bare, and ~/obd2/deploy/set-gpu-cma.sh does not yet exist on the box -- i.e. the deploy has not run. The story ships the repo-managed mechanism; the drill (deploy -> reboot -> `grep CmaTotal /proc/meminfo`, expect ~262144 kB) closes AC2. The script prints exactly that command and that expected number, and deliberately says REBOOT REQUIRED rather than implying the pool was raised immediately -- claiming otherwise would be a confident lie about a value anyone can read. HONEST BOUND ON THE STORY ITSELF: this is Atlas RCA #4, OPTIONAL HEADROOM. It is NOT a fix for the freeze class -- US-522's --disable-gpu is. Do not read a green US-524 as 'the freeze is fixed', and note the interaction: with --disable-gpu the kiosk renders in software, so a larger CMA pool may show no measurable effect on chromium at all. The value of the raise is margin for the KMS/display stack generally, and I am not claiming a measured benefit nobody has measured. (2) It is deliberately not tag-driven: the loop-control contract rewritten 2026-05-12 (ralph.sh header) states 'The continue/stop decision is derived from sprint.json state, NOT from the model's <promise> tag. The tag is advisory only' and explicitly lists '<promise>COMPLETE</> when the count disagrees ... CONTINUE'. (3) PARTIAL_BLOCKED's documented behaviour IS this loop's default (continue to the next iteration), so a branch would be a literal no-op; ralph.sh step 5 already names it in the keep-going bucket. (4) THE LITERAL DRIFT, which is the smoking gun: ralph.sh's header documents the tags with the ABBREVIATED closing form `<promise>COMPLETE</>` (line ~16), invisible to the test's `</promise>` regex -- I dumped every occurrence in the file with its line number, comment flag and grep flag to confirm this rather than assume it. WHY THE BRANCH IS REFUSED: `grep -q '<promise>COMPLETE</promise>' -> exit 0` would let a model END A SPRINT BY ASSERTING COMPLETION while stories are still passes:false. That is precisely the failure the 2026-05-12 rewrite removed, and it is the worst class of bug for this harness -- it would look like it works and silently truncate sprints. So the absence is now PINNED as a test (test_completeTagIsNotAGrepBranch_soAModelCannotEndASprintByAssertingIt) rather than left as an implicit convention a future 'fix TD-073' pass would undo. BUT THE OBVIOUS ALTERNATIVE -- LOOSENING THE GATE -- IS THE RUBBER STAMP THE AC FORBIDS, so I took neither branch of the false dichotomy. The old parser counted ANY full-form tag string anywhere in ralph.sh as 'handled', which is a weak proxy in both directions: it MISSES real handling written in the abbreviated form, and it can be SATISFIED BY A COMMENT. Simply adding a comment would have turned the suite green while the gate learned nothing. So the gate was RE-GROUNDED, not relaxed, and the net result is STRICTER than before: it now parses (i) REAL grep branches -- comment lines are stripped FIRST, so prose that merely mentions a tag (or the word 'grep') can never masquerade as a branch -- against (ii) explicit `# NOT_TAG_DRIVEN: <promise>X</promise> -- <why>` declarations in ralph.sh, and asserts every documented tag is accounted for exactly once, with no ghost branch (a branch for a tag Ralph is never told to emit), no ghost declaration (a declaration for a tag prompt.md never documents), and no tag that is BOTH (a contradiction that would make the declaration a lie). The NOT_TAG_DRIVEN hatch alone could be silenced without the loop actually being able to end a sprint, so test_ralphShEndsTheSprintFromTheSprintJsonTally_notFromTheTag pins the MECHANISM: the tally comparison, the 'PRD COMPLETE' announcement, and an `exit 0` within the branch.
